title: Phase 11 — LLM Engineering Checkpoint
description: Optional checkpoint after Phase 11: prompting, structured outputs, and RAG fundamentals. Never blocks curriculum access.

options: Conditioning the model at inference time with worked examples
Adding a system prompt with rules
questions.explanation: Few-shot inference conditions behaviour via examples in the prompt; no training happens unless you fine-tune separately.

questions.prompt: When you need machine-parseable output, using a constrained structured-output format (e.g. JSON schema) is more reliable than parsing free-form prose.
questions.explanation: Schema-constrained outputs reduce parsing failures and ambiguity versus parsing natural language responses.

questions.prompt: In a RAG evaluation, recall@k measures:
options: How often the mailed answer is correct
The fraction of required source chunks that appear in the top-k retrieved set
How diverse the retrieved chunks are
questions.explanation: Recall@k is a retrieval metric: of the chunks a query needs, how many make it into the top-k

questions.prompt: Increasing chunk overlap when chunking documents most directly trades off:
options: Index size vs answer correctness — more overlap usually hurts retrieval granularity
questions.explanation: Bigger overlap shrinks unique content per chunk and can obscure boundaries, while slightly helping continuity; it should be treated as an ablation, and measured

questions.prompt: A RAG answer generated without grounding in the retrieved context should be labelled enforced-at-architecture-level rather than prompted politely.
questions.explanation: Grounding (constraint via prompt structure, retrieval-only context, refusal paths) is an architectural safeguard; soft prompting weakly guides but does not enforce.

questions.prompt: Order a RAG pipeline's stages into their logical flow:
options: Generate an answer grounded in the retrieved chunks
questions.explanation: Chunk, embed, retrieve, generate: you can't retrieve un-embedded chunks and can't generate grounded text without retrieved context.

questions.prompt: Select every practice that makes LLM evaluation results more trustworthy:
options: Fixed evaluation sets versioned in the repo
Tuning prompts on the test set directly
questions.explanation: Versioning, provenance, and honest failure reporting build trust; tuning on the eval set inflates results.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between retrieval failure and generation failure in a RAG pipeline and give one symptom of each.

criteria: Distinguishes retrieval (wrong/missing context) from generation (wrong use of good context)
Symptom of retrieval failure: correct-looking answer to the wrong question OR missed grounding
Symptom of generation failure: answer contradicts the retrieved chunks

questions.explanation: Retrieval failure gives the model context that doesn't contain the answer (symptom: confident but unsupported claims or correct answers to an adjacent question). Generation failure has good chunks but the model doesn't use them (symptom: answer contradicts cited chunks).
